# wiremock - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wiremock/^0.6/

## Expand description

`wiremock` provides HTTP mocking to perform black-box testing of Rust applications that
interact with third-party APIs.

It provides mocking of HTTP responses using request matching and response templating.

[§](https://docs.rs#how-to-install)How to install

Add `wiremock` to your development dependencies:

```
[dev-dependencies]
# ...
wiremock = "0.5"
```
If you are using [ cargo-edit](https://github.com/killercup/cargo-edit), run

`cargo add wiremock --dev`[§](https://docs.rs#getting-started)Getting started

```
use wiremock::{MockServer, Mock, ResponseTemplate};
use wiremock::matchers::{method, path};
#[async_std::main]
async fn main() {
    // Start a background HTTP server on a random local port
    let mock_server = MockServer::start().await;
    // Arrange the behaviour of the MockServer adding a Mock:
    // when it receives a GET request on '/hello' it will respond with a 200.
    Mock::given(method("GET"))
        .and(path("/hello"))
        .respond_with(ResponseTemplate::new(200))
        // Mounting the mock on the mock server - it's now effective!
        .mount(&mock_server)
        .await;

    // If we probe the MockServer using any HTTP client it behaves as expected.
    let status = reqwest::get(format!("{}/hello", &mock_server.uri()))
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .status();
    assert_eq!(status, 200);
    // If the request doesn't match any `Mock` mounted on our `MockServer` a 404 is returned.
    let status = reqwest::get(format!("{}/missing", &mock_server.uri()))
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .status();
    assert_eq!(status, 404);
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#matchers)Matchers

`wiremock` provides a set of matching strategies out of the box - check the [ matchers](https://docs.rs/matchers/index.html) module
for a complete list.

You can define your own matchers using the [ Match](https://docs.rs/trait.Match.html) trait, as well as using

`Fn` closures.Check

[’s documentation for more details and examples.](https://docs.rs/trait.Match.html)

`Match`[§](https://docs.rs#spying)Spying

`wiremock` empowers you to set expectations on the number of invocations to your [ Mock](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html)s -
check the

[method for more details.](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html#method.expect)

`expect`Expectations can be used to verify that a side-effect has (or has not) taken place!

Expectations are automatically verified during the shutdown of each [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/struct.MockServer.html) instance,
at the end of your test. A failed verification will trigger a panic.

By default, no expectations are set on your

[s.](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html)

`Mock`[§](https://docs.rs#responses)Responses

`wiremock` lets you specify pre-determined responses using [ ResponseTemplate](https://docs.rs/struct.ResponseTemplate.html) and

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.MockBuilder.html#method.respond_with)

`respond_with`You also given the option to have [ Mock](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html)s that return different responses based on the matched

[using the](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html)

`Request`[trait.](https://docs.rs/trait.Respond.html)

`Respond`Check

[’s documentation for more details and examples.](https://docs.rs/trait.Respond.html)

`Respond`[§](https://docs.rs#test-isolation)Test isolation

Each instance of [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/struct.MockServer.html) is fully isolated:

[takes care of finding a random port available on your local machine which is assigned to the new](https://docs.rs/struct.MockServer.html#method.start)

`start`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.MockServer.html)

`MockServer`To ensure full isolation and no cross-test interference, [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/struct.MockServer.html)s shouldn’t be
shared between tests. Instead,

[s should be created in the test where they are used.](https://docs.rs/struct.MockServer.html)

`MockServer`When a [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/struct.MockServer.html) instance goes out of scope (e.g. the test finishes), the corresponding
HTTP server running in the background is shut down to free up the port it was using.

[§](https://docs.rs#runtime-compatibility)Runtime compatibility

`wiremock` can be used (and it is tested to work) with both [ async_std](https://docs.rs/async-std/) and

[as futures runtimes.](https://docs.rs/tokio/)

`tokio`If you encounter any compatibility bug, please open an issue on our

[GitHub repository](https://github.com/LukeMathWalker/wiremock-rs).

[§](https://docs.rs#efficiency)Efficiency

`wiremock` maintains a pool of mock servers in the background to minimise the number of
connections and the time spent starting up a new [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/struct.MockServer.html).

Pooling reduces the likelihood of you having to tune your OS configurations (e.g. ulimit).

The pool is designed to be invisible: it makes your life easier and your tests faster. If you end up having to worry about it, it’s a bug: open an issue!

[§](https://docs.rs#prior-art)Prior art

[ mockito](https://docs.rs/mockito/) and

[provide HTTP mocking for Rust.](https://docs.rs/httpmock/)

`httpmock`Check the table below to see how `wiremock` compares to them across the following dimensions:

- Test execution strategy (do tests have to be executed sequentially or can they be executed in parallel?);
- How many APIs can I mock in a test?
- Out-of-the-box request matchers;
- Extensible request matching (i.e. you can define your own matchers);
- Sync/Async API;
- Spying (e.g. verify that a mock has/hasn’t been called in a test);
- Standalone mode (i.e. can I launch an HTTP mock server outside of a test suite?).

| Test execution strategy | How many APIs can I mock? | Out-of-the-box request matchers | Extensible request matching | API | Spying | Standalone mode | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| mockito | ❌ Sequential | ❌ 1 | ✔ | ❌ | Sync | ✔ | ❌ |
| httpmock | ✔ Parallel | ✔ Unbounded | ✔ | ✔ | Async/Sync | ✔ | ✔ |
| wiremock | ✔ Parallel ️ | ✔ Unbounded | ✔ | ✔ | Async | ✔ | ❌ |

[§](https://docs.rs#future-evolution)Future evolution

More request matchers can be added to those provided out-of-the-box to handle common usecases.

# yew-nav-link 0.10.8 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/yew-nav-link/0.10.8

# yew-nav-link

Enterprise-grade navigation library for [Yew](https://yew.rs) — automatic active state detection and a complete component system.

[ 🌐 Live demo →](https://raprogramm.github.io/yew-nav-link/) —

**📖 Architectural book →***Click a  NavLink — the route changes, and the active class plus aria-current="page" follow automatically.*

## Table of Contents

- [Overview](https://docs.rs#overview)
- [Installation](https://docs.rs#installation)
- [Requirements](https://docs.rs#requirements)
- [Quick Start](https://docs.rs#quick-start)
- [Components](https://docs.rs#components)
- [CSS Integration](https://docs.rs#css-integration)
- [Architecture](https://docs.rs#architecture)
- [Examples](https://docs.rs#examples)
- [API Reference](https://docs.rs#api-reference)
- [Migration Guides](https://docs.rs#migration-guides)
- [Coverage](https://docs.rs#coverage)
- [Contributing](https://docs.rs#contributing)
- [License](https://docs.rs#license)

## Overview

`yew-nav-link` is a comprehensive navigation library for the Yew web framework. It provides:

| Feature | Description |
|---|---|
| NavLink | Drop-in replacement for Yew Router's `<Link>`with automatic`active`class detection |
| Component System | 15+ ready-to-use UI components (tabs, dropdowns, pagination, badges, icons) |
| Hooks | Reactive hooks for route state, active checking, breadcrumbs, and programmatic navigation |
| Utilities | Path manipulation, URL encoding, keyboard navigation, and query string handling |
| Customization | Custom CSS classes, programmatic navigation, and extensible breadcrumb providers |

The core `NavLink` component eliminates manual active state tracking. It compares the current route against the target on every render and applies the `active` CSS class automatically — zero configuration required.

```
[]
 = "0.10"
```

|---|---|
| Rust | 1.96+ |
| Edition | 2024 |
| Yew | 0.23+ |
| yew-router | 0.20+ |

### Component Syntax

```
use *;
use NavLink;
use *;
```
When the user visits `/about`, the second link automatically receives `class="nav-link active"`.

### Partial Matching

Keep parent links highlighted on nested routes:

```
html!
```
Partial matching is segment-aware: `/docs` matches `/docs/api` but **not** `/documentation`.

### Custom CSS Classes

Customize the default `nav-link` and `active` classes:

```

```
### Programmatic Navigation

`use_navigation::<R>()` returns a [`Navigation<R>`] handle exposing pre-built `Callback`s — no manual `Callback::from(...)` boilerplate.

```
use *;
use use_navigation;
```
### Custom Breadcrumb Providers

Implement [`BreadcrumbLabelProvider`] to control how each path segment is rendered. The provider operates on **paths** (e.g. `/docs/api`), not on `Routable` enum variants — it works the same for static and parameterised routes.

```
use Rc;
use ;
;
```

|---|---|---|

| `use_is_exact_active(route)` | `bool` | Whether the route matches exactly |
| `use_is_partial_active(route)` | `bool` | Whether the route is a prefix of the current path |

## Architecture

```
yew-nav-link
├── active_link       # Core NavLink component + Match enum
├── nav               # Primitives: NavList, NavItem, NavDivider
├── components        # UI: Badge, Dropdown, Icon, Tabs, Pagination
├── hooks             # Reactive and programmatic route/navigation helpers
├── utils             # Path, URL, keyboard navigation utilities
├── attrs             # Type-safe attribute builders
└── errors            # NavError, NavResult types
```

# yew - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/yew/^0.23/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#yew-framework---api-documentation)Yew Framework - API Documentation

Yew is a modern Rust framework for creating multi-threaded front-end web apps using WebAssembly

- Features a macro for declaring interactive HTML with Rust expressions. Developers who have experience using JSX in React should feel quite at home when using Yew.
- Achieves high performance by minimizing DOM API calls for each page render and by making it easy to offload processing to background web workers.
- Supports JavaScript interoperability, allowing developers to leverage NPM packages and integrate with existing JavaScript applications.

[§](https://docs.rs#supported-targets-client-side-rendering)Supported Targets (Client-Side Rendering)

- `wasm32-unknown-unknown`

[§](https://docs.rs#note)Note

Server-Side Rendering should work on all targets when feature `ssr` is enabled.

[§](https://docs.rs#supported-features)Supported Features:

- `csr`: Enables Client-side Rendering support and- `Renderer`
- `ssr`: Enables Server-side Rendering support and- `ServerRenderer`
- `hydration`: Enables Hydration support.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use yew::prelude::*;
enum Msg {
    AddOne,
}
struct App {
    value: i64,
}
impl Component for App {
    type Message = Msg;
    type Properties = ();
    fn create(ctx: &Context<Self>) -> Self {
        Self { value: 0 }
    }
    fn update(&mut self, _ctx: &Context<Self>, msg: Self::Message) -> bool {
        match msg {
            Msg::AddOne => {
                self.value += 1;
                true
            }
        }
    }
    fn view(&self, ctx: &Context<Self>) -> Html {
        html! {
            <div>
                <button onclick={ctx.link().callback(|_| Msg::AddOne)}>{ "+1" }</button>
                <p>{ self.value }</p>
            </div>
        }
    }
}
fn main() {
    yew::Renderer::<App>::new().render();
}
```

# yew_router - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/yew-router/^0.20/

## Expand description

Provides routing faculties using the browser history API to build
Single Page Applications (SPAs) using [Yew web framework](https://yew.rs).

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

```
use yew::functional::*;
use yew::prelude::*;
use yew_router::prelude::*;
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Routable)]
enum Route {
    #[at("/")]
    Home,
    #[at("/secure")]
    Secure,
    #[not_found]
    #[at("/404")]
    NotFound,
}
#[component(Secure)]
fn secure() -> Html {
    let navigator = use_navigator().unwrap();
    let onclick_callback = Callback::from(move |_| navigator.push(&Route::Home));
    html! {
        <div>
            <h1>{ "Secure" }</h1>
            <button onclick={onclick_callback}>{ "Go Home" }</button>
        </div>
    }
}
#[component(Main)]
fn app() -> Html {
    html! {
        <BrowserRouter>
            <Switch<Route> render={switch} />
        </BrowserRouter>
    }
}
fn switch(routes: Route) -> Html {
    match routes {
        Route::Home => html! { <h1>{ "Home" }</h1> },
        Route::Secure => html! {
            <Secure />
        },
        Route::NotFound => html! { <h1>{ "404" }</h1> },
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#internals)Internals

The router registers itself as a context provider and makes location information and navigator
available via [ hooks](https://docs.rs/hooks/index.html) or

[.](https://docs.rs/scope_ext/trait.RouterScopeExt.html)

`RouterScopeExt`[§](https://docs.rs#state)State

The [ Location](https://docs.rs/history/struct.Location.html) API has a way to access / store state associated with
session history. Please consult

[for detailed usage.](https://docs.rs/history/struct.Location.html#method.state)

# wasm_bindgen_futures - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-bindgen-futures/^0.4/

## Expand description

Bridging the gap between Rust Futures and JavaScript Promises.

This crate is now a thin shim re-exporting from [ js_sys::futures](https://docs.rs/js-sys/0.3.103/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/js_sys/futures/index.html).
The implementation has been moved into

`js-sys` so that
[can implement](https://docs.rs/js-sys/0.3.103/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/js_sys/struct.Promise.html)

`js_sys::Promise`[directly, enabling](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/future/into_future/trait.IntoFuture.html)

`core::future::IntoFuture``promise.await` without any wrapper type.All public items (`JsFuture`, `spawn_local`, `future_to_promise`,
`future_to_promise_typed`) are re-exported unchanged for backwards
compatibility.

# web_sys - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/web-sys/^0.3/

## Expand description

Raw API bindings for Web APIs

This is a procedurally generated crate from browser WebIDL which provides a binding to all APIs that browsers provide on the web.

This crate by default contains very little when compiled as almost all of
its exposed APIs are gated by Cargo features. The exhaustive list of
features can be found in `crates/web-sys/Cargo.toml`, but the rule of thumb
for `web-sys` is that each type has its own cargo feature (named after the
type). Using an API requires enabling the features for all types used in the
API, and APIs should mention in the documentation what features they
require.

# criterion - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/criterion/^0.8/

## Expand description

A statistics-driven micro-benchmarking library written in Rust.

This crate is a microbenchmarking library which aims to provide strong statistical confidence in detecting and estimating the size of performance improvements and regressions, while also being easy to use.

See
[the user guide](https://criterion-rs.github.io/book/index.html)
for examples as well as details on the measurement and analysis process,
and the output.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features:

- Collects detailed statistics, providing strong confidence that changes to performance are real, not measurement noise.
- Produces detailed charts, providing thorough understanding of your code’s performance behavior.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [async_](https://docs.rs/async_executor/index.html)- executor
- This module defines a trait that can be used to plug in different Futures executors into Criterion.rs’ async benchmarking support.
- [measurement](https://docs.rs/measurement/index.html)
- This module defines a set of traits that can be used to plug different measurements (eg.
Unix’s Processor Time, CPU or GPU performance counters, etc.) into Criterion.rs. It also
includes the `WallTime`
- [profiler](https://docs.rs/profiler/index.html)
- This module provides an extension trait which allows in-process profilers
to be hooked into the `--profile-time`argument at compile-time. Users of out-of-process profilers such as perf don’t need to do anything special.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [criterion_](https://docs.rs/macro.criterion_group.html)- group
- Macro used to define a function group for the benchmark harness; see the
`criterion_main!`
- [criterion_](https://docs.rs/macro.criterion_main.html)- main
- Macro which expands to a benchmark harness.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Async](https://docs.rs/struct.AsyncBencher.html)- Bencher
- Async/await variant of `Bencher`
- [Bencher](https://docs.rs/struct.Bencher.html)
- Timer struct used to iterate a benchmarked function and measure the runtime.
- [Benchmark](https://docs.rs/struct.BenchmarkGroup.html)- Group
- Structure used to group together a set of related benchmarks, along with custom configuration settings for groups of benchmarks. All benchmarks performed using a benchmark group will be grouped together in the final report.
- [Benchmark](https://docs.rs/struct.BenchmarkId.html)- Id
- Simple structure representing an ID for a benchmark. The ID must be unique within a benchmark group.
- [Criterion](https://docs.rs/struct.Criterion.html)
- The benchmark manager
- [Plot](https://docs.rs/struct.PlotConfiguration.html)- Configuration
- Contains the configuration options for the plots generated by a particular benchmark or benchmark group.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Axis](https://docs.rs/enum.AxisScale.html)- Scale
- Axis scaling type. Specified via `PlotConfiguration::summary_scale`
- [Baseline](https://docs.rs/enum.Baseline.html)
- Baseline describes how the `baseline_directory`is handled.
- [Batch](https://docs.rs/enum.BatchSize.html)- Size
- Argument to `Bencher::iter_batched``Bencher::iter_batched_ref`
- [Benchmark](https://docs.rs/enum.BenchmarkFilter.html)- Filter
- Benchmark filtering support.
- [Plotting](https://docs.rs/enum.PlottingBackend.html)- Backend
- Enum used to select the plotting backend.
- [Sampling](https://docs.rs/enum.SamplingMode.html)- Mode
- This enum allows the user to control how Criterion.rs chooses the iteration count when sampling.
The default is `Auto`, which will choose a method automatically based on the iteration time during the warm-up phase.
- [Throughput](https://docs.rs/enum.Throughput.html)
- Enum representing different ways of measuring the throughput of benchmarked code. If the throughput setting is configured for a benchmark then the estimated throughput will be reported as well as the time per iteration.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [black_](https://docs.rs/fn.black_box.html)- box - Deprecated
- A function that is opaque to the optimizer, used to prevent the compiler from optimizing away computations in a benchmark.

# proptest - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/proptest/^1/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#proptest-reference-documentation)Proptest Reference Documentation

This is the reference documentation for the proptest API.

For documentation on how to get started with proptest and general usage
advice, please refer to the [Proptest Book](https://proptest-rs.github.io/proptest/intro.html).

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [arbitrary](https://docs.rs/arbitrary/index.html)
- Defines the `Arbitrary`trait and related free functions and type aliases.
- [array](https://docs.rs/array/index.html)
- Support for strategies producing fixed-length arrays.
- [bits](https://docs.rs/bits/index.html)
- Strategies for working with bit sets.
- [bool](https://docs.rs/bool/index.html)
- Strategies for generating `bool`values.
- [char](https://docs.rs/char/index.html)
- Strategies for generating `char`values.
- [collection](https://docs.rs/collection/index.html)
- Strategies for generating `std::collections`of values.
- [num](https://docs.rs/num/index.html)
- Strategies to generate numeric values (as opposed to integers used as bit fields).
- [option](https://docs.rs/option/index.html)
- Strategies for generating `std::Option`values.
- [path](https://docs.rs/path/index.html)- `std`
- Strategies for generating [`PathBuf`] and related path types.
- [prelude](https://docs.rs/prelude/index.html)
- Re-exports the most commonly-needed APIs of proptest.
- [range_](https://docs.rs/range_subset/index.html)- subset - `std`
- Strategies for generating values by taking samples of index ranges.
- [result](https://docs.rs/result/index.html)
- Strategies for combining delegate strategies into `std::Result`s.
- [sample](https://docs.rs/sample/index.html)
- Strategies for generating values by taking samples of collections.
- [strategy](https://docs.rs/strategy/index.html)
- Defines the core traits used by Proptest.
- [string](https://docs.rs/string/index.html)- `std`
- Strategies for generating strings and byte strings from regular expressions.
- [test_](https://docs.rs/test_runner/index.html)- runner
- State and functions for running proptest tests.
- [tuple](https://docs.rs/tuple/index.html)
- Support for combining strategies into tuples.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [prop_](https://docs.rs/macro.prop_assert.html)- assert
- Similar to `assert!`from std, but returns a test failure instead of panicking if the condition fails.
- [prop_](https://docs.rs/macro.prop_assert_eq.html)- assert_ - eq
- Similar to `assert_eq!`from std, but returns a test failure instead of panicking if the condition fails.
- [prop_](https://docs.rs/macro.prop_assert_ne.html)- assert_ - ne
- Similar to `assert_ne!`from std, but returns a test failure instead of panicking if the condition fails.
- [prop_](https://docs.rs/macro.prop_assume.html)- assume
- Rejects the test input if assumptions are not met.
- [prop_](https://docs.rs/macro.prop_compose.html)- compose
- Convenience to define functions which produce new strategies.
- [prop_](https://docs.rs/macro.prop_oneof.html)- oneof
- Produce a strategy which picks one of the listed choices.
- [proptest](https://docs.rs/macro.proptest.html)
- Easily define `proptest`tests.

## Attribute Macros[§](https://docs.rs#attributes)

- [property_](https://docs.rs/attr.property_test.html)- test - `attr-macro`
- The `property_test`procedural macro simplifies the creation of property-based tests using the`proptest`crate. This macro provides a more concise syntax for writing tests that automatically generate test cases based on properties.

# yew_nav_link - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/yew-nav-link/0.10.8/target-redirect/yew_nav_link/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#yew-nav-link)yew-nav-link

Navigation link component for [Yew](https://yew.rs) with automatic active
state detection.

[§](https://docs.rs#overview)Overview

`yew-nav-link` provides a [ NavLink](https://docs.rs/active_link/nav_link/struct.NavLink.html) component that wraps Yew Router’s

`Link` with automatic active state management. When the target route matches
the current URL, an `active` CSS class is applied.[§](https://docs.rs#quick-start)Quick Start

```
[dependencies]
yew-nav-link = "0.10"
```
[§](https://docs.rs#component-syntax)Component Syntax

```
use yew::prelude::*;
use yew_nav_link::NavLink;
use yew_router::prelude::*;
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Debug, Routable)]
enum Route {
    #[at("/")]
    Home,
    #[at("/about")]
    About
}
#[component]
fn Navigation() -> Html {
    html! {
        <nav>
            <NavLink<Route> to={Route::Home}>{ "Home" }</NavLink<Route>>
            <NavLink<Route> to={Route::About}>{ "About" }</NavLink<Route>>
        </nav>
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#function-syntax)Function Syntax

For text-only links, use [ nav_link()](https://docs.rs/active_link/nav_link/fn.nav_link.html) with explicit

[mode:](https://docs.rs/active_link/mode/enum.Match.html)

`Match````
use yew::prelude::*;
use yew_nav_link::{Match, nav_link};
use yew_router::prelude::*;
#[component]
fn Menu() -> Html {
    html! {
        <nav>
            { nav_link(Route::Home, "Home", Match::Exact) }
            { nav_link(Route::Docs, "Docs", Match::Partial) }
        </nav>
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#partial-matching)Partial Matching

Use `partial` prop to keep parent links active on nested routes:

```
use yew::prelude::*;
use yew_nav_link::NavLink;
use yew_router::prelude::*;
#[component]
fn Navigation() -> Html {
    html! {
        <nav>
            // Active on /docs, /docs/api, /docs/*
            <NavLink<Route> to={Route::Docs} partial=true>{ "Docs" }</NavLink<Route>>
        </nav>
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#css-classes)CSS Classes

| Class | Condition |
|---|---|
| `nav-link` | Always |
| `active` | Route matches |

Compatible with Bootstrap, Tailwind, and other CSS frameworks.

[§](https://docs.rs#requirements)Requirements

- Yew 0.23+
- yew-router 0.20+

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use active_link::`- [Match](https://docs.rs/active_link/mode/enum.Match.html);
- `pub use components::`- [PageItem](https://docs.rs/components/struct.PageItem.html);
- `pub use components::`- [PageItemProps](https://docs.rs/components/struct.PageItemProps.html);
- `pub use components::`- [PageLink](https://docs.rs/components/struct.PageLink.html);
- `pub use components::`- [PageLinkProps](https://docs.rs/components/struct.PageLinkProps.html);

# yew_nav_link - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/yew-nav-link/0.10.8/yew_nav_link/index.html

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#yew-nav-link)yew-nav-link

Navigation link component for [Yew](https://yew.rs) with automatic active
state detection.

[§](https://docs.rs#overview)Overview

`yew-nav-link` provides a [ NavLink](https://docs.rs/active_link/nav_link/struct.NavLink.html) component that wraps Yew Router’s

`Link` with automatic active state management. When the target route matches
the current URL, an `active` CSS class is applied.[§](https://docs.rs#quick-start)Quick Start

```
[dependencies]
yew-nav-link = "0.10"
```
[§](https://docs.rs#component-syntax)Component Syntax

```
use yew::prelude::*;
use yew_nav_link::NavLink;
use yew_router::prelude::*;
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Debug, Routable)]
enum Route {
    #[at("/")]
    Home,
    #[at("/about")]
    About
}
#[component]
fn Navigation() -> Html {
    html! {
        <nav>
            <NavLink<Route> to={Route::Home}>{ "Home" }</NavLink<Route>>
            <NavLink<Route> to={Route::About}>{ "About" }</NavLink<Route>>
        </nav>
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#function-syntax)Function Syntax

For text-only links, use [ nav_link()](https://docs.rs/active_link/nav_link/fn.nav_link.html) with explicit

[mode:](https://docs.rs/active_link/mode/enum.Match.html)

`Match````
use yew::prelude::*;
use yew_nav_link::{Match, nav_link};
use yew_router::prelude::*;
#[component]
fn Menu() -> Html {
    html! {
        <nav>
            { nav_link(Route::Home, "Home", Match::Exact) }
            { nav_link(Route::Docs, "Docs", Match::Partial) }
        </nav>
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#partial-matching)Partial Matching

Use `partial` prop to keep parent links active on nested routes:

```
use yew::prelude::*;
use yew_nav_link::NavLink;
use yew_router::prelude::*;
#[component]
fn Navigation() -> Html {
    html! {
        <nav>
            // Active on /docs, /docs/api, /docs/*
            <NavLink<Route> to={Route::Docs} partial=true>{ "Docs" }</NavLink<Route>>
        </nav>
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#css-classes)CSS Classes

| Class | Condition |
|---|---|
| `nav-link` | Always |
| `active` | Route matches |

Compatible with Bootstrap, Tailwind, and other CSS frameworks.

[§](https://docs.rs#requirements)Requirements

- Yew 0.23+
- yew-router 0.20+

# yew_nav_link - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/yew-nav-link

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#yew-nav-link)yew-nav-link

Navigation link component for [Yew](https://yew.rs) with automatic active
state detection.

[§](https://docs.rs#overview)Overview

`yew-nav-link` provides a [ NavLink](https://docs.rs/active_link/nav_link/struct.NavLink.html) component that wraps Yew Router’s

`Link` with automatic active state management. When the target route matches
the current URL, an `active` CSS class is applied.[§](https://docs.rs#quick-start)Quick Start

```
[dependencies]
yew-nav-link = "0.10"
```
[§](https://docs.rs#component-syntax)Component Syntax

```
use yew::prelude::*;
use yew_nav_link::NavLink;
use yew_router::prelude::*;
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Debug, Routable)]
enum Route {
    #[at("/")]
    Home,
    #[at("/about")]
    About
}
#[component]
fn Navigation() -> Html {
    html! {
        <nav>
            <NavLink<Route> to={Route::Home}>{ "Home" }</NavLink<Route>>
            <NavLink<Route> to={Route::About}>{ "About" }</NavLink<Route>>
        </nav>
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#function-syntax)Function Syntax

For text-only links, use [ nav_link()](https://docs.rs/active_link/nav_link/fn.nav_link.html) with explicit

[mode:](https://docs.rs/active_link/mode/enum.Match.html)

`Match````
use yew::prelude::*;
use yew_nav_link::{Match, nav_link};
use yew_router::prelude::*;
#[component]
fn Menu() -> Html {
    html! {
        <nav>
            { nav_link(Route::Home, "Home", Match::Exact) }
            { nav_link(Route::Docs, "Docs", Match::Partial) }
        </nav>
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#partial-matching)Partial Matching

Use `partial` prop to keep parent links active on nested routes:

```
use yew::prelude::*;
use yew_nav_link::NavLink;
use yew_router::prelude::*;
#[component]
fn Navigation() -> Html {
    html! {
        <nav>
            // Active on /docs, /docs/api, /docs/*
            <NavLink<Route> to={Route::Docs} partial=true>{ "Docs" }</NavLink<Route>>
        </nav>
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#css-classes)CSS Classes

| Class | Condition |
|---|---|
| `nav-link` | Always |
| `active` | Route matches |

Compatible with Bootstrap, Tailwind, and other CSS frameworks.

[§](https://docs.rs#requirements)Requirements

- Yew 0.23+
- yew-router 0.20+

# NavLink in yew_nav_link::active_link::nav_link - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/yew-nav-link/0.10.8/yew_nav_link/active_link/nav_link/struct.NavLink.html

Navigation link with automatic active-state detection.

Renders an <a> tag and intercepts left-clicks to push the target route
through yew_router’s Navigator. Modifier-clicks (Cmd/Ctrl/Shift/Alt
or middle-click) fall through to the browser, preserving the standard
“open in new tab” affordance.

When the route matches, the rendered anchor gains:

the active class (or whatever active_class overrides it with), and

aria-current="page" so screen readers announce the current location.

---

# nav_link in yew_nav_link::active_link::nav_link - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/yew-nav-link/0.10.8/yew_nav_link/active_link/nav_link/fn.nav_link.html

`pub fn nav_link<R: `[Routable](https://docs.rs/yew-router/0.20.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/yew_router/routable/trait.Routable.html) + [PartialEq](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cmp/trait.PartialEq.html) + [Clone](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/clone/trait.Clone.html) + 'static>(
    to: R,
    children: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    match_mode: [Match](https://docs.rs/mode/enum.Match.html),
) -> [Html](https://docs.rs/yew/0.23.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/yew/html/type.Html.html)## Expand description

Creates a `NavLink` with the specified match mode for plain-text labels.

`match_mode` selects between exact and prefix matching:

- `Match::Exact`- `to`.
- `Match::Partial`- `to.to_path()`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use yew::prelude::*;
use yew_nav_link::{Match, nav_link};
use yew_router::prelude::*;
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Debug, Routable)]
enum Route {
    #[at("/")]
    Home,
    #[at("/docs")]
    Docs,
    #[at("/docs/api")]
    DocsApi
}
#[function_component]
fn Menu() -> Html {
    html! {
        <nav>
            { nav_link(Route::Home, "Home", Match::Exact) }
            { nav_link(Route::Docs, "Docs", Match::Partial) }
        </nav>
    }
}
```

The NavLink component and the nav_link function-syntax helper.

Both build on the same active-state algorithm: compare the current route
to the target on every render and toggle the active class plus
aria-current="page" accordingly.
